Project Activities 4.1 Electrolyte Optimization (UMD) A ZnCl₂ + NaCl high-entropy electrolyte (HEE) extended the electrochemical stability to ~2.1 V while maintaining high ionic conductivity. A bio-safe additive, 4-hydroxy-3- methoxybenzaldehyde (HE), suppressed hydrogen evolution and improved Zn plating/stripping reversibility at both 0.5 and 2 mA cm⁻². Transition to ZnSO₄-based electrolytes enabled stainless- steel current collectors by eliminating Cl⁻-induced corrosion while preserving high CE. 4.2 Zn-Pulp Ion Conductor and Cathode Development (Yale & WHP) Cellulose treated in Zn–NaOH formed a Zn-CNF-II network with enhanced mechanical strength and ion transport. As a binder and membrane, Zn-CNF enabled uniform thick MnO₂ electrodes. Dry-compression yielded crack-free, current-collector-free pellets up to 250 mg cm⁻²; for optimal energy and cost balance, 60 mg cm⁻² slurry-cast cathodes were selected. 4.3 Pouch-Cell Fabrication and Testing (WHP) Using Zn-CNF membranes and HEE/modified electrolytes, >100 mAh pouch cells were assembled. Stainless-steel collectors with SO₄²⁻-based HEE delivered up to ~98% capacity retention after 80 cycles at C/5. Root causes of fading (Zn dendrites, electrolyte infiltration dynamics) were identified via post-mortem examinations and mitigated via pre-soaking and additive tuning. 4.4 Cost and Tech-to-Market Activities (WHP) A design-based techno-economic model linked cell architecture to delivered $/kWh. Replacing carbon cloth with stainless steel and adopting slurry coating reduced materials cost and simplified manufacturing. Engagements with EverZinc, Salient Energy, BASF, Octet, and USDA FPL advanced supply-chain readiness and scale-up pathways. 5. Project Outputs A. Conclusion The WHP–UMD–Yale collaboration met the principal objectives of the CREATE effort: a safe, low-cost Zn-pulp battery with wide-temperature operability and a validated <$30/kWh cost pathway. Electrolyte innovations (HEE + HE additive), robust Zn-CNF ion conductors, and thick MnO₂ cathodes were demonstrated in pouch cells. Remaining challenges—thick-electrode cycling stability and Zn dendrite suppression—are the focus of proposed continuation efforts. The program established a strong foundation for commercialization of low-cost, non-flammable, long-duration zinc batteries for stationary storage.
